title: The View of the War From a Florida Gas Station

sentences.zh: 就是这样，兄弟。

sentences.zh: 你能解释一下你接下来要做什么吗？

sentences.en: I'm going to raise the gas price.
sentences.zh: 我要调高油价。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: So we got to go into the fuel manager menu and fuel price configuration.
sentences.zh: 我们得进入燃油管理菜单和燃油价格配置。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: I'm going to go from $449 on my premium to $469.
sentences.zh: 我要把高级汽油的价格从4.49美元调到4.69美元。

sentences.en: For the past four weeks, gas stations across the United States have become a kind of microcosm of the war's domestic impact.
sentences.zh: 过去四周里，全美的加油站已成为战争对国内影响的一种缩影。

sentences.en: It's there at thousands of pumps and cash registers that a test of wills is playing out in real time.
sentences.zh: 正是在成千上万的加油泵和收银台前，一场意志的较量正在实时上演。

sentences.en: I just got to download the fuel prices to my pumps, and that's that.
sentences.zh: 我只需要把燃油价格下载到加油泵上，这就行了。

sentences.en: Price increased.
sentences.zh: 价格已上调。

sentences.en: Between gas station managers deciding day after day just how much to charge for a gallon of gas,
sentences.zh: 在加油站经理日复一日地决定每加仑汽油卖多少钱，

sentences.en: and already cash-strapped consumers deciding just how much pain they're willing to endure.
sentences.zh: 以及本已捉襟见肘的消费者决定他们愿意承受多少痛苦之间。

sentences.en: I mean, does any part of you just feel, like, really bad that you have to do that?
sentences.zh: 我是说，你内心深处有没有觉得，不得不这样做真的很糟糕？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 有。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I feel bad.
sentences.zh: 我感觉很糟糕。

sentences.en: I mean, it's a necessity.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这是必需的。

sentences.en: I have to.
sentences.zh: 我必须这么做。

sentences.en: But, yeah, I feel bad.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，我感觉很糟糕。

sentences.en: That kind of hurts.
sentences.zh: 那确实让人难受。

sentences.en: Today, the view of this war from a neighborhood gas station in Jacksonville, Florida.
sentences.zh: 今天，从佛罗里达州杰克逊维尔的一家社区加油站来看这场战争。

sentences.en: It's Friday, March 27th.
sentences.zh: 今天是3月27日，星期五。

sentences.en: I think this is it.
sentences.zh: 我想就是这个了。

sentences.en: Yeah, here we go.
sentences.zh: 对，开始了。

sentences.en: Yo, we're getting there.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我们快到了。

sentences.en: Hey, Florida.
sentences.zh: 嘿，佛罗里达。

sentences.en: Florida drivers.
sentences.zh: 佛罗里达的司机们。

sentences.en: Last week, Daily Producer Anna Foley and I headed to suburban Jacksonville to talk to a gas station manager named Cam Judy.
sentences.zh: 上周，我和《每日新闻》的制片人安娜·福利前往杰克逊维尔郊区，采访了一位名叫卡姆·朱迪的加油站经理。

sentences.en: Hey, guys.
sentences.zh: 嘿，大家好。

sentences.en: What's going on?
sentences.zh: 最近怎么样？

sentences.en: Welcome here.
sentences.zh: 欢迎光临。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: Michael.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔。

sentences.en: Cameron.
sentences.zh: 卡梅伦。

sentences.en: Cameron, nice to meet you.
sentences.zh: 卡梅伦，很高兴见到你。

sentences.en: Nice to meet you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴见到你。

sentences.en: Now, why this station and this manager?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么选择这家加油站和这位经理呢？

sentences.en: Oh, we can come on back?
sentences.zh: 哦，我们可以到后面去吗？

sentences.en: Okay, great.
sentences.zh: 好的，太棒了。

sentences.en: Because Cam runs a quickly vanishing business in this country, an independently owned gas station.
sentences.zh: 因为卡姆经营着这个国家正在迅速消失的一种生意：独立经营的加油站。

sentences.en: You got some serious Little Debbie.
sentences.zh: 你这儿有很棒的Little Debbie零食。

sentences.en: Serious Little Debbie stuff, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，是很正宗的Little Debbie。

sentences.en: Yeah, right there, right in front, staring at me across the way all day, whispering my name.
sentences.zh: 是啊，就在那儿，就在正前方，整天盯着我，在我耳边低语我的名字。

sentences.en: Honey buns.
sentences.zh: 蜂蜜小圆面包。

sentences.en: Meaning that Cam and Cam alone sets the price.
sentences.zh: 这意味着卡姆，只有卡姆一个人在定价。

sentences.en: I've never been in the guts of the cashier's wing of the store.
sentences.zh: 我从来没进过这家店收银台的内部。

sentences.en: We met him on a Tuesday when regular unleaded gas at his station cost $3.79 a gallon, about 40% higher than before the war started.
sentences.zh: 我们是在周二见到他的，当时他店里的普通无铅汽油价格是每加仑3.79美元，比战争开始前高出约40%。

sentences.en: Cam was manning the cash register of the station's convenience store.
sentences.zh: 卡姆当时正在便利店的收银台值班。

sentences.en: And it's inside this store on a residential street across from an elementary school where you really see how intimately he's woven himself into this community.
sentences.zh: 在这家位于小学对面居民街上的店里，你真的能看出他与这个社区的联系有多么紧密。

sentences.en: What's up, Rick?
sentences.zh: 怎么了，里克？

sentences.en: Mr. Lee.
sentences.zh: 李先生。

sentences.en: Hey, Lewis.
sentences.zh: 嘿，刘易斯。

sentences.en: Yeah, you're good, brother.
sentences.zh: 没错，你做得很好，兄弟。

sentences.en: Are you on a first-name basis with a lot of customers?
sentences.zh: 你和很多顾客都直呼其名吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, after eight years, almost nine years this July, it'll be nine years.
sentences.zh: 是啊，八年了，今年七月就快九年了。

sentences.en: I got a lot of regulars that come in here.
sentences.zh: 有很多常客会来这里。

sentences.en: Cam took over the business about a decade ago from his father, who started buying convenience stores after he immigrated to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 卡姆大约十年前从他父亲手中接过了这家生意，他父亲在从叙利亚经危地马拉移民到美国后，开始收购便利店。

sentences.en: from Syria by way of Guatemala.
sentences.zh: 从叙利亚经危地马拉。

sentences.en: This gas station in particular he bought right around the time my sister was born, I believe.
sentences.zh: 我想，这家加油站是他大约在我妹妹出生时买下的。

sentences.en: Seems to be a trend.
sentences.zh: 这似乎成了一种趋势。

sentences.en: He has a kid, he has a gas station.
sentences.zh: 他有了孩子，就有了加油站。

sentences.en: He has a kid, he has a gas station.
sentences.zh: 他有了孩子，就有了加油站。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: And Cam grew up watching his father really become the unofficial mayor of this neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 卡姆从小看着他父亲真正成为了这个社区的非正式市长。

sentences.en: He always goes back to the show Everybody Loves Raymond.
sentences.zh: 他总是提到《人人都爱雷蒙德》这部剧。

sentences.en: That's his name, Raymond.
sentences.zh: 那就是他的名字，雷蒙德。

sentences.en: So even growing up as a kid, we couldn't go out to eat without running into somebody that he knew from one of the stores.
sentences.zh: 所以即使小时候，我们出去吃饭也总会碰到他从店里认识的人。

sentences.en: A waiter, somebody in the back cooking our food in the kitchen, somebody waiting in line for their coffee.
sentences.zh: 服务员、在后厨做饭的人，或者排队买咖啡的人。

sentences.en: He knows everybody.
sentences.zh: 他认识所有人。

sentences.en: And it went beyond just knowing everybody.
sentences.zh: 而且这不仅仅是认识所有人那么简单。

sentences.en: His father's customers were treated as an extension of the Judy family.
sentences.zh: 他父亲把顾客当作朱迪家族的延伸来对待。

sentences.en: I didn't know the extent of my dad's impact on some of these customers until I started working here
sentences.zh: 直到我开始在这里工作，我才知道我父亲对其中一些顾客的影响有多大，

sentences.en: when someone would come in here and tell me, like, you know, your dad, like, I was, my power was off.
sentences.zh: 当有人进来告诉我，你知道吗，你父亲，比如，我当时，我的电被停了。

sentences.en: And he loaned me the money I needed to get the electricity back on, you know, and stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 他借给我钱让我交电费，你知道，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: It's like, Dad, did you really do that?
sentences.zh: 我就想，爸爸，你真的那样做了吗？

sentences.en: He's like, of course I did.
sentences.zh: 他说，我当然做了。

sentences.en: They've been coming to my store for 10, 15 years.
sentences.zh: 他们来我的店里已经10年、15年了。

sentences.en: So for Cam, this was really the only way he knew to run a business.
sentences.zh: 所以对卡姆来说，这是他唯一知道的经营方式。

sentences.en: These regular customers that I get in here, I mean, I've known them now for eight years.
sentences.zh: 这些常客，我是说，我已经认识他们八年了。

sentences.en: That's a longer time than I've known my kids.
sentences.zh: 这比我认识我孩子的时间还长。

sentences.en: I only got a four-year-old.
sentences.zh: 我只有一个四岁的孩子。

sentences.en: So some of these people, they've been around for my wife's pregnancies.
sentences.zh: 所以这些人中，有些见证了我妻子的怀孕过程。

sentences.en: I had several regular customers when they found out my wife was pregnant.
sentences.zh: 我妻子怀孕时，有几位常客发现了。

sentences.en: They brought me boxes and boxes and boxes of diapers.
sentences.zh: 他们给我送来了好几箱好几箱的尿布。

sentences.en: Like, it's just really cool.
sentences.zh: 这真的很酷。

sentences.en: I don't think a lot of people get to experience that, where a customer comes to your business almost every single day,
sentences.zh: 我觉得很多人没有机会体验这种感觉，顾客几乎每天都来你的店里，

sentences.en: sometimes up to six times a day, and become a huge part of your life.
sentences.zh: 有时一天来六次，成为了你生活中很重要的一部分。

sentences.en: They really do.
sentences.zh: 他们确实是。

sentences.en: And just to give you an example, when Cam catches local students shoplifting, which happens with some frequency, he never calls the police.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，当卡姆抓到当地学生偷东西时（这种情况时有发生），他从不报警。

sentences.en: He tells somebody else.
sentences.zh: 他会告诉别人。

sentences.en: I know their P.E.
sentences.zh: 我认识他们的体育老师。

sentences.en: coach.
sentences.zh: 老师。

sentences.en: He comes in here every day.
sentences.zh: 他每天都来这里。

sentences.en: So I tell him, I show him a picture of the kid on my camera, and he makes them run laps.
sentences.zh: 所以我告诉他，给他看我监控里拍到的孩子照片，他就会让那孩子去跑圈。

sentences.en: Or push-ups.
sentences.zh: 或者做俯卧撑。

sentences.en: Get out of here.
sentences.zh: 走开。

sentences.en: That's local justice.
sentences.zh: 这就是地方正义。

sentences.en: I love it.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这样。

sentences.en: So when the war broke out a few weeks ago...
sentences.zh: 所以当几周前战争爆发时……

sentences.en: Right before the war, I remember we were sitting at $279 for a long time.
sentences.zh: 战争爆发前，我记得我们的油价在很长一段时间里都保持在2.79美元。

sentences.en: And Cam realized he was going to have to raise gas prices.
sentences.zh: 卡姆意识到他不得不提高油价。
从2.79美元涨到2.99美元，再到3.09美元。

sentences.en: Over and over.
sentences.zh: 一次又一次。

sentences.en: We went up almost 20 cents in 48 hours.
sentences.zh: 我们在48小时内涨了近20美分。

sentences.en: And over again.
sentences.zh: 又一次。

sentences.en: Gosh, it's been almost every day.
sentences.zh: 天哪，几乎每天都在涨。

sentences.en: He wasn't repeatedly raising gas prices on strangers.
sentences.zh: 他并不是在反复对陌生人涨价。

sentences.en: He was raising prices on people he really cares about.
sentences.zh: 他是在对他真正关心的人涨价。

sentences.en: People who he knows are already stretched very thin.
sentences.zh: 那些他知道本已生活拮据的人。

sentences.en: I hope they understand that I'm not pricing my gas to make a quick buck.
sentences.zh: 我希望他们明白，我调高油价不是为了赚快钱。

sentences.en: I'm pricing my gas how I need to price it in order to stay afloat.
sentences.zh: 我调高油价是因为为了维持经营，我必须这样做。

sentences.en: And just to explain how this works, this is actually not making Cam more money.
sentences.zh: 为了解释这是怎么运作的，其实这并没有让卡姆赚更多钱。

sentences.en: My distributor of fuel is charging me per gallon.
sentences.zh: 我的燃油供应商是按加仑向我收费的。

sentences.en: And then I have to account for if they're going to charge me to get it to the gas station.
sentences.zh: 然后我还得考虑他们是否会收取运费。

sentences.en: Trucking fees.
sentences.zh: 运输费。

sentences.en: Trucking fees to the store itself.
sentences.zh: 运到店里的运输费。

sentences.en: And then we also have to account for the different fees that are associated with the customer purchasing gas.
sentences.zh: 然后我们还得考虑顾客购买燃油时产生的各种费用。

sentences.en: The credit card companies and debit card companies.
sentences.zh: 信用卡公司和借记卡公司的手续费。

sentences.en: For Cam, the margins on gas are actually pretty slim.
sentences.zh: 对卡姆来说，燃油的利润空间其实非常薄。

sentences.en: I mean, there's really such a small amount of profit to be made per gallon for a business like mine.
sentences.zh: 我是说，像我这样的生意，每加仑能赚的利润真的很少。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm talking maybe 10 to 15 cents per gallon max for my store.
sentences.zh: 我是说，每加仑最多也就赚10到15美分。

sentences.en: His pumps hold about 8,000 gallons, which usually lasts a couple of weeks.
sentences.zh: 他的油罐大约能装8,000加仑，通常能用几周。

sentences.en: And so 10 cents of profit on that is about $800, which is a surprisingly small amount of profit for a gas station to make on gas.
sentences.zh: 所以每加仑10美分的利润大约是800美元，对于加油站来说，这笔利润少得惊人。

sentences.en: How did you think about this question of how much you could increase the price of the pump knowing your customer?
sentences.zh: 在了解你顾客的情况下，你是如何思考调高油价这个问题的？

sentences.en: How did you balance all that?
sentences.zh: 你是如何平衡这一切的？

sentences.en: I mean, my regular customers, they're pretty loyal.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我的常客们都很忠诚。

sentences.en: I like to think that they would choose my store over a big corporate-owned gas station, a big chain gas station franchise like that, just because it's my store.
sentences.zh: 我愿意相信，他们会选择我的店，而不是那种大型企业拥有的加油站，那种大型连锁加油站，仅仅因为这是我的店。

sentences.en: Can I consider the customer when I'm making these gas prices?
sentences.zh: 我在定价时能考虑顾客吗？

sentences.en: Not really, because as much as I love my regular customers, I can't take a loss per gallon.
sentences.zh: 不能，因为尽管我爱我的常客，但我不能亏本卖油。

sentences.en: I can't – it would be even – it would be difficult to even figure out what my break-even number would be.
sentences.zh: 我不能——甚至很难算出我的保本点是多少。

sentences.en: You know, we've got to at least make a couple cents off of each gallon or there's really no point in –
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们每加仑至少得赚几美分，否则就真的没有意义了——

sentences.en: Selling gas.
sentences.zh: 卖油。

sentences.en: Selling gas.
sentences.zh: 卖汽油。

sentences.en: I could take the gas price of that big chain gas station up the road that's priced at $3.99 today.
sentences.zh: 我可以把价格定得跟路那头那家大型连锁加油站一样，今天他们卖3.99美元。

sentences.en: I could say, well, I'm independently owned.
sentences.zh: 我可以想，嗯，我是独立经营的。

sentences.en: I need to have a bigger profit margin and price mine for $4.09.
sentences.zh: 我需要更高的利润空间，所以我定价4.09美元。

sentences.en: I could do that.
sentences.zh: 我可以这么做。

sentences.en: You know, there's no problem with me doing that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我这么做也没什么问题。

sentences.en: I know gas station owners that do do that.
sentences.zh: 我认识的加油站老板里确实有人这么做。

sentences.en: They go 10 cents over their nearest big corporate gas station just so that they can make a little bit more of a profit margin.
sentences.zh: 他们会比附近的大型企业加油站多加10美分，就为了能多赚一点利润。

sentences.en: I choose not to, specifically because of the relationship I have with my regular customers.
sentences.zh: 我选择不这样做，主要是因为我和老顾客之间有感情。

sentences.en: I would love for this to be over next week and I go back to $2.79 a gallon.
sentences.zh: 我真希望下周这一切就能结束，价格能回到每加仑2.79美元。

sentences.en: That would be awesome.
sentences.zh: 那太棒了。

sentences.en: I hope beyond hope that it is temporary and it does not last long.
sentences.zh: 我无比希望这只是暂时的，不会持续太久。

sentences.en: But yeah, I do worry about the longevity of these high prices.
sentences.zh: 但说实话，我确实担心这些高价会持续很久。

sentences.en: It would be a strain on a lot of people, myself included.
sentences.zh: 这对很多人来说都是一种负担，包括我自己。

sentences.en: But despite his best intentions, as we wrapped up our conversation and Cam's day came to an end, he checks in on prices around town.
sentences.zh: 尽管他本意并非如此，但在我们结束谈话、Cam的一天即将结束时，他还是查看了城里的油价。

sentences.en: Most of his rivals were at $3.99 a gallon for regular.
sentences.zh: 他的大多数竞争对手普通汽油的价格都是每加仑3.99美元。

sentences.en: He had been holding steady at $3.79.
sentences.zh: 而他一直稳在3.79美元。

sentences.en: He looks out at the pumps.
sentences.zh: 他看向加油泵。

sentences.en: I don't like to do it when customers are pumping gas.
sentences.zh: 我不喜欢在顾客加油的时候调价。

sentences.en: And he makes the call to raise the prices.

sentences.zh: 那每一块钱都花得心疼。

sentences.en: It's hard right now.
sentences.zh: 现在真的很难。

sentences.en: That's what I'm trying to tell you.
sentences.zh: 这就是我想告诉你的。

sentences.en: Like, on top of grocery.
sentences.zh: 就像，还要加上买菜钱。

sentences.en: On top of rent.
sentences.zh: 还要加上房租。

sentences.en: Because, I mean, I pay $2,000 to live.
sentences.zh: 因为，我是说，我每个月要付2000美元的房租。

sentences.en: Every month.
sentences.zh: 每个月。

sentences.en: Now we're talking about gas.
sentences.zh: 现在又加上油费。

sentences.en: I have the ride to work.
sentences.zh: 我得开车去上班。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: I have grandchildren.
sentences.zh: 我有孙辈。

sentences.en: I have two elderly parents that live in my home.
sentences.zh: 我有两位年迈的父母住在我家里。

sentences.en: One of them who has stage 5 kidney disease.
sentences.zh: 其中一位患有5期肾病。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: And I just took him to dialysis.
sentences.zh: 我刚带他去做了透析。

sentences.en: So even with incomes, it's going like this.
sentences.zh: 所以即使有收入，钱也是这样流失的。

sentences.en: You're down the drain.
sentences.zh: 你就像掉进了下水道。

sentences.en: Down the drain.
sentences.zh: 彻底完了。

sentences.en: You said you were excited for $2 gas.
sentences.zh: 你说你曾为2美元的油价感到兴奋。

sentences.en: Like...
sentences.zh: 就像……

sentences.en: Oh my God!
sentences.zh: 天哪！

sentences.en: I was like, we are here!
sentences.zh: 我当时想，我们终于熬出头了！

sentences.en: And was that something you heard from the president in his campaigns?
sentences.zh: 那是你在总统竞选时听到的承诺吗？

sentences.en: Was that where you heard that from?
sentences.zh: 你是从那儿听说的吗？

sentences.en: Trump said that we were going to have lower gas.
sentences.zh: 特朗普说我们会享受到更低的油价。

sentences.en: That was one of the things that he promised.
sentences.zh: 那是他承诺的事情之一。

sentences.en: And unfortunately, I voted for him.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，我投票给了他。

sentences.en: As a black woman, I voted for this man thinking that our economy is going to be amazing under him.
sentences.zh: 作为一个黑人女性，我投票给这个人，以为在他的领导下我们的经济会变得非常棒。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And?
sentences.zh: 然后呢？

sentences.en: And now I wish I never did that.
sentences.zh: 现在我真希望我从没投过他。

sentences.en: Are you mad that he started this war and raised...
sentences.zh: 你是因为他发动了这场战争并提高了……而感到愤怒吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Because to me now, it's not even about people no more.
sentences.zh: 因为对我来说，现在这已经不再关乎人命了。

sentences.en: It's about money.
sentences.zh: 这关乎金钱。

sentences.en: I know we are in America and we think we're safe, but we're casualties of war.
sentences.zh: 我知道我们身在美国，觉得很安全，但我们其实是战争的牺牲品。

sentences.en: We have to start speaking out against what's going on over there.
sentences.zh: 我们必须开始公开反对那边正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: Because we will be them if we don't stand up for them.
sentences.zh: 因为如果我们不为他们挺身而出，我们就会成为下一个受害者。

sentences.en: You're upset.
sentences.zh: 你很心烦。

sentences.en: I'm upset.
sentences.zh: 我很心烦。

sentences.en: I mean, you're crying.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你在哭。

sentences.en: I'm upset.
sentences.zh: 我很心烦。

sentences.en: Do you feel like you were kind of hoodwinked?
sentences.zh: 你觉得你是被骗了吗？

sentences.en: Yes, I was hoodwinked.
sentences.zh: 是的，我被骗了。

sentences.en: This man talked about we were going to be great again.
sentences.zh: 这个人说我们要让美国再次伟大。

sentences.en: And I did kind of see that in my eyes.
sentences.zh: 我当时确实是这么认为的。

sentences.en: It's like we were not the America that we used to be.
sentences.zh: 感觉我们不再是以前那个美国了。

sentences.en: So, okay, we have this man coming through and he's bold and he's powerful.
sentences.zh: 所以，好吧，有这么一个人出现，他大胆且强大。

sentences.en: He pumped me up off of I'm a good man.
sentences.zh: 他用“我是个好人”那一套打动了我。

sentences.en: But then he really was a wolf in sheep's clothing.
sentences.zh: 但实际上他披着羊皮的狼。

sentences.en: I got everything I want.
sentences.zh: 我得到了我想要的一切。

sentences.en: I got your vote.
sentences.zh: 我得到了你的选票。

sentences.en: And now I'm just going to tear it down.
sentences.zh: 现在我要把一切都毁掉。

sentences.en: It's all about me and my money and my big rich friends.
sentences.zh: 这全是为了我，为了我的钱，为了我那些有钱的朋友。

sentences.en: So, I'm upset.
sentences.zh: 所以我很心烦。

sentences.en: I made the wrong vote.
sentences.zh: 我投错了票。

sentences.en: And I need everybody to understand what we're going through.
sentences.zh: 我需要让每个人都了解我们正在经历什么。

sentences.en: Like, stop.
sentences.zh: 停下吧。

sentences.en: We are not on the beach anymore.
sentences.zh: 我们已经不在海滩上度假了。

sentences.en: Take your shades off.
sentences.zh: 摘下你的墨镜吧。

sentences.en: The tsunami hit.
sentences.zh: 海啸已经来了。

sentences.en: And it was called President Trump.
sentences.zh: 它叫特朗普总统。

sentences.en: We got to get up.
sentences.zh: 我们得站起来。

sentences.en: I'm a proud American.
sentences.zh: 我是一个自豪的美国人。

sentences.en: Very, very proud American.
sentences.zh: 非常、非常自豪的美国人。

sentences.en: And right today, I'm a sad American.
sentences.zh: 但今天，我是一个悲伤的美国人。

sentences.en: I'm not real proud.
sentences.zh: 我一点也不感到自豪。

sentences.en: So, I'm not real proud of us.
sentences.zh: 所以，我真的为我们感到羞愧。

sentences.en: Well, thank you for sharing.
sentences.zh: 好吧，谢谢你的分享。

sentences.en: Take care.
sentences.zh: 保重。

sentences.en: So, I think we're wrapping up KMAR reporting at the gas station.
sentences.zh: 那么，我想我们在加油站的KMAR报道就到此结束了。

sentences.en: And I wonder if you can forecast a little bit in the next week and whether you think you're going to have to keep raising prices.
sentences.zh: 我想问你能不能预测一下下周的情况，你觉得你还得继续涨价吗？

sentences.en: What it would take for you to lower them.
sentences.zh: 要达到什么条件你才会降价？

sentences.en: I don't see lowering happening anytime soon.
sentences.zh: 我看不出短期内会有降价的可能。

sentences.en: Usually, when it's quick to rise like this, it's slower to lower.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，涨价很快，降价却很慢。

sentences.en: I don't think it's going to take a week for me to have to raise it, honestly, above $399.
sentences.zh: 老实说，我觉得用不了一周我就得把价格涨到3.99美元以上了。

sentences.en: As I was driving into work today, I passed by a gas station charging $405 for credit card purchases on gasoline.
sentences.zh: 今天开车上班时，我路过一家加油站，他们的信用卡汽油价格是4.05美元。

sentences.en: Regular.
sentences.zh: 普通汽油。

sentences.en: Regular.
sentences.zh: 普通汽油。

sentences.en: And it was an independent as well.
sentences.zh: 那也是一家独立加油站。

sentences.en: Same as mine.
sentences.zh: 跟我的一样。

sentences.en: Probably over the weekend, I'll probably have to go above $4.
sentences.zh: 可能周末我就得涨到4美元以上了。

sentences.en: And as far as going well beyond $4, I could see it capping around $459.
sentences.zh: 至于涨到4美元以上多少，我估计上限会在4.59美元左右。

sentences.en: That's my estimated price cap, I believe.
sentences.zh: 我相信这就是我的预估价格上限。

sentences.en: How do you come up with that number?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么得出这个数字的？

sentences.en: That's probably the highest that I remember ever putting my gas prices at.
sentences.zh: 这可能是我记忆中我把油价定得最高的一次了。

sentences.en: I hope it doesn't get to $459.
sentences.zh: 我希望它不会涨到4.59美元。

sentences.en: I hope it doesn't go above $409.
sentences.zh: 我希望它不会超过4.09美元。

sentences.en: But as unpredictable as everything is and what's going on, you just never know.
sentences.zh: 但鉴于一切都变幻莫测，局势动荡，你永远无法预料会发生什么。

sentences.en: Well, thank you again for all the time you've given us.
sentences.zh: 好的，再次感谢你们抽出时间接受我们的采访。

sentences.en: I appreciate y'all coming out here and talking to me about this.
sentences.zh: 我很感激你们能来到这里和我谈论这些。

sentences.en: Till next time.
sentences.zh: 下次见。

sentences.en: Yes, sir.
sentences.zh: 是的，先生。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是您今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: They now have the chance, that is Iran, to permanently abandon their nuclear ambitions and to turn a new path forward.
sentences.zh: 伊朗现在有机会永久放弃其核野心，并开辟一条新的前进道路。

sentences.en: We'll see if they want to do it.
sentences.zh: 我们拭目以待他们是否愿意这样做。

sentences.en: On Thursday, President Trump sought to ratchet up pressure on Iran to enter into diplomatic negotiations to end the war.
sentences.zh: 周四，特朗普总统试图加大对伊朗的压力，迫使其进行外交谈判以结束战争。

sentences.en: If they don't, we're their worst nightmare.
sentences.zh: 如果他们不这样做，我们就是他们最可怕的噩梦。

sentences.en: In the meantime, we'll just keep blowing them away, unimpeded, unstopped.
sentences.zh: 在此期间，我们将继续打击他们，不受阻碍，绝不停止。

sentences.en: Trump's latest threat came as Israel claimed it had killed a key Iranian naval commander who had led Iran's effort to close the Strait of Hormuz and as Israel expanded its ground operations in Lebanon.
sentences.zh: 特朗普发出最新威胁之际，以色列声称击毙了一名伊朗海军关键指挥官，此人曾领导伊朗试图封锁霍尔木兹海峡，同时以色列也扩大了在黎巴嫩的地面行动。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, the crisis at America's airports could soon come to an end after the Senate voted early Friday morning to reopen the Department of Homeland Security,
sentences.zh: 与此同时，美国机场的危机可能很快就会结束，因为参议院周五凌晨投票决定重新开放国土安全部，

sentences.en: which has been shut down for weeks.
sentences.zh: 该部门已经关闭了数周。

sentences.en: The bill, which now heads to the House, would fund every major DHS operation, including airport security, except for immigration enforcement.
sentences.zh: 该法案现已提交众议院，将为国土安全部的所有主要业务提供资金，包括机场安检，但移民执法除外。

sentences.zh: 今天的节目由安娜·福利和凯特琳·奥基夫制作。

sentences.zh: 由德文·泰勒剪辑。

sentences.zh: 包含丹·鲍威尔、黛安·王、艾丽西亚·布蒂特普、马里昂·洛萨诺和切尔西·丹尼尔的音乐。

sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonderly创作。

sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一台严密控制的机器一样运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了一批自称改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直陷入一场激烈、混乱，有时又令人兴奋的斗争之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的《地铁》节目中，我，莎拉·凯尼格，将为您讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。
